mentions.author: dannygarcia
mentions.story: Ask HN: What are the best advanced computer science courses online?
mentions.text:
I would say Roughgarden's four CS Algorithms courses on Coursera are somewhat more advanced than CS50: [course]

It covers foundational topics like asymptotic notation. However there is some reading required if you a C in high school calculus like me.

mentions.author: ctoomey
mentions.story: Ask HN: Which Coursera courses/specializations you recommend?
mentions.text: The Stanford algorithms specialization ( [course]) is outstanding. Professor Roughgarden is the best instructor I've ever had, online or in person. He's got infectious enthusiasm about the topic and does a great job explaining the algorithms and how to analyze and understand them.

mentions.author: rst_noimage
mentions.story: Ask HN: If I've already taught myself to code, should I still get my CS degree?
mentions.text: I have CS degree and what i feel is if you already taught yourself code, you passed step 1, but I think to go to next level please focus on more Algorithm Analysis part first example Coursera -> [course]. It will take a while if you have full-time job but consistency is what it matters. Once you comfortable with those concept then move to more advance distributed system areas.

mentions.author: imakecomments
mentions.story: Want a Job in Silicon Valley? Keep Away from Coding Schools
mentions.text:
I recommend learning discrete mathematics, then data structures and algorithms.

I cannot stress enough how important mathematical foundations is. It'll make everything else much easier to learn. I haven't read the book but heard good things about: [link] as a beginner text.

Coursera has multiple offerings on Data Structures / Algorithms -- find one that works best for you.

For instance:

[course]

[course]

[course]

[course]

By doing all of those you'll get a good introductory exposure to the topics.

You should also look at a rigorous course offering of Algorithms. MIT has a few online to view.
